body:
## Finding

The #317 punctuation-safe review exposed a three-record lipoic-acid family whose labels, stereochemistry, and CAS provenance are inconsistent.

| preferred term | occurrences | current target | current CAS | finding |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `(DL)-alpha-Lipoic acid` | 1,399 | CHEBI:16494 `lipoic acid` | 1077-28-7 | coherent stereo-unspecified/racemic anchor |
| `Thioctic acid` | 30 | CHEBI:30314 `(R)-lipoic acid` | 1077-28-7 | CAS denotes the generic/(±) material and is not an xref on the R target |
| `α-lipoic acid` | 4 | CHEBI:43796 `(S)-lipoic acid` | 1077-27-6 | source label is stereo-unspecified; S CAS/structure were derived from the chosen ontology target, not independent source evidence |

Local ChEBI data gives CHEBI:30314 CAS 1200-22-2 / 62-46-4, while CHEBI:16494 carries `Thioctic acid` and `alpha-lipoic acid` aliases. The `α-lipoic acid` record also stores `D,L-6,8-Thioctic Acid` as a synonym, directly conflicting with an S-only identity.

This is not a mapping-quality-only correction: the current targets themselves need source-level review. The revised #317 regrader therefore holds these out instead of converting them mechanically.

## Scope

- Trace the 30 `Thioctic acid` and 4 `α-lipoic acid` occurrences back to source recipe labels/registry rows.
- Determine whether either source actually specifies R/S material; do not infer stereochemistry from a target-derived CAS, InChI, or synonym.
- Reground stereo-unspecified labels to CHEBI:16494 unless independent source evidence supports an enantiomer.
- Correct/remove CAS and structure fields whose only provenance is the rejected target.
- Decide whether the generic records should merge with `(DL)-alpha-Lipoic acid` or remain source-distinct aliases; preserve occurrence provenance either way.
- Reconcile SSSOM and generated artifacts after curation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every lipoic/thioctic record has source-backed stereochemistry.
- [ ] CAS RN agrees with the selected stereochemical identity and ChEBI xrefs.
- [ ] No target-derived property is cited as independent evidence for retaining that same target.
- [ ] Generic/racemic and R/S identities are not collapsed without explicit source evidence.
- [ ] Duplicate/merge decisions preserve all occurrences and curation history.
- [ ] A regression check flags a stereospecific target when the source label is unspecified and all specificity evidence was ontology-derived.

Related: #317 (surfaced during identity-bearing punctuation review); #230 (precedent for separating stereochemical senses).
title: Resolve lipoic/thioctic stereochemistry: generic labels are grounded to R/S targets and one CAS contradicts its target
